portInfo.description: Puerto Chiapas on Mexico’s far southern Pacific coast is administered by ASIPONA Puerto Chiapas (site branding also references Puerto Madero). The authority’s terminals page states a specialised cruise terminal planned for tourist ships up to 311 metres LOA and 15,000 TRB alongside a 150-metre quay with facilities designed for cruise operations. An English-language port news feature highlights distinctive wood-and-palm architecture and tropical surroundings. The port also publishes a cruise arrivals calendar PDF linked from the site navigation. This is a different Pacific Mexican call from Puerto Vallarta or Ensenada — do not reuse those guides’ transfer assumptions.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Check the port’s published cruise arrivals calendar PDF before assuming weekly calls — Puerto Chiapas volumes are not interchangeable with Mexican Riviera hubs.
